extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comedy fans, comedians and TV producers interested in the Roast Battle / Jeff Ross Presents Roast Battle format
extracted.subtask_description: Format, rules, and procedural requirements for the televised roast-comedy competition 'Jeff Ross Presents Roast Battle', including how battles are run, judged, and how contestants are selected. Useful for comedians, producers, or fans wanting the show's constraints and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only original material
rubrics_metrics.description: The competitors must use only original material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the show's three explicit rules; implies that recycled or 'stolen' jokes are disallowed in battle performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: No physical contact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the show's three explicit rules; enforces that battles are verbal/performative rather than physical, with a referee present to enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battle ends with a hug
rubrics_metrics.description: The battle always ends with a hug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the show's three explicit rules; sets an expectation of sportsmanship and closure after the insults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast-comedy content: insult each other comedically
rubrics_metrics.description: One-on-one roast battles during which the comedians would insult each other comedically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the genre/acceptable tone of material — direct insults delivered for comedic effect rather than other forms of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner determination by guest-judge panel
rubrics_metrics.description: The winners of each battle were decided by a panel of guest judges that consisted of fellow comedians and other celebrities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is subjective and performed by a rotating panel; the page notes panels include 'two or more comedians or other celebrities' and that the host (Jeff Ross) also serves as one of the judges on each show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge panel composition (comedians/celebrities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest judges include fellow comedians and other celebrities; typically two or more per battle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the expected background of judges (industry peers/celebrities), which shapes evaluation norms and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bracket-style tournament selection (regional-to-finals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional events and bracket-style tournaments were used to determine contestants for the main competition (e.g., search across Los Angeles, Austin, Chicago, New York City into a final bracket).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the typical selection/competition structure for seasons 1–2: regionals feed into a final sixteen and then final eight via elimination brackets; season 3 abandoned the bracket-style tournament and changed to two battles per episode without prelim regionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible finalist selection (direct additions allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to regionals, some comedians were added directly to the final sixteen and did not compete in regionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates selection is not strictly limited to regional winners; producers can add contestants directly to later rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcer/referee role to enforce format
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedian Brian Moses served as the announcer and referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The referee/announcer role is a formal production element responsible for introductions and enforcing rules (e.g., preventing physical contact), contributing to the procedural fairness of each battle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finals sometimes broadcast live
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rounds (final battle) were broadcast live on Comedy Central in at least one season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live broadcast increases stakes and may affect performance style, content sensitivity, and production logistics.
